benefits: Catches bad API payloads before they crash your app: validate the shape, not just the syntax.
Documents your data contract: the schema is a readable specification of what is allowed.
Speeds up debugging: every violation lists its exact path and a plain-language reason.
Tests edge cases safely: try the failing sample to see all five rule types fire at once.
Runs fully in your browser: production payloads are never uploaded to a server.

faqs.a: A JSON document that describes the allowed shape of another JSON document: which properties are required, what types they must have, and which constraints (lengths, ranges, patterns) apply.

No - this tool implements the widely used subset: types, required, properties, additionalProperties, string/number/array constraints, enum, const, and the allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not combinators. Exotic keywords like $ref, $dynamicRef, and format assertions are not supported.
faqs.q: Does it support the full JSON Schema specification?

faqs.a: Yes. Both the schema and the instance must be valid JSON first. A broken schema reports its own parse error before any validation runs.
faqs.q: Does it check that my schema itself is valid JSON?

faqs.a: When a value has the wrong type, deeper checks are skipped to avoid noise - for example a string where a number was expected reports only the type error, not the range errors.
faqs.q: Why do I see only one error for a wrong-typed value?

faqs.a: Yes. required lists the properties that must exist; properties describes the allowed ones. With additionalProperties: false, any other key is rejected.
faqs.q: Can I require some fields and forbid unknown ones?

faqs.a: Use oneOf when exactly one alternative must match (for example circle vs rectangle), anyOf when at least one must match, and allOf when every subschema must hold at once.
faqs.q: When do I use oneOf vs anyOf vs allOf?

json-schema-validator.formula:
validate(value, schema, path):
  type check      -> mismatch stops deeper checks (avoids noise)
  enum / const    -> value must equal an allowed value
  string          -> minLength, maxLength, pattern (regex)
  number          -> minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum/Maximum, multipleOf, integer
  array           -> minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, items (per-index or single)
  object          -> required, properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties
  combinators     -> allOf (every), anyOf (>= 1), oneOf (exactly 1), not (none)
howTo: Paste your JSON Schema into the schema box (a sample is preloaded).
Paste the JSON document to check into the instance box.
Validation runs live: a green badge means valid, a red badge lists every violation.
Each violation shows its path (like $.age) and a plain-language reason.
Use the sample buttons to toggle between a passing and a failing document.
keyFacts: JSON Schema describes the allowed shape of JSON data: types, required fields, and constraints.
This tool implements the practical subset: types, required, properties, additionalProperties, string/number/array limits, enum, const, and allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not.
Every violation reports a JSONPath-like location (for example $.address.zip) plus a readable message.
A type mismatch stops deeper checks on that value so one mistake produces one clear error.
Both the schema and the instance must be valid JSON before validation runs.
Validation messages are shown in your chosen language: English, Hindi, or Arabic.
json-schema-validator.keywords: json schema validator, validate json against schema, json schema checker, json schema tester online

labels.validLabel: Valid: the instance matches the schema.

limitations: Implements the common subset only: $ref, $dynamicRef, recursive schemas, and format assertions are not supported.
Error messages describe the first problem per value; deeply broken documents may need several fix-and-recheck rounds.
Number precision follows JavaScript doubles; huge integers may lose precision during parsing.
Very large schemas or instances may be slow since validation runs on the main thread.

messages.allOf: Value does not satisfy every allOf subschema.
messages.anyOf: Value does not match any of the anyOf subschemas.
messages.const: Value does not match the required constant.
messages.enum: Value is not one of the allowed enum values.
messages.falseSchema: Value is not allowed here (schema is false).
messages.invalidPattern: Schema pattern '{pattern}' is not a valid regular expression.
messages.maxItems: Array has more than maxItems ({max}) items.
messages.maxProperties: Object has more than maxProperties ({max}) properties.
messages.maximum: Number {value} is greater than the maximum {max}.
messages.minItems: Array has fewer than minItems ({min}) items.
messages.minProperties: Object has fewer than minProperties ({min}) properties.
messages.minimum: Number {value} is less than the minimum {min}.
messages.multipleOf: Number {value} is not a multiple of {base}.
messages.oneOf: Value must match exactly one subschema (matched {count}).
messages.pattern: String does not match the required pattern.

json-schema-validator.workedExample:
Schema requires name (non-empty string) and age (integer 0-150), with no extra properties.

Passing instance: {"name":"Asha Sharma","age":30} -> Valid.

Failing instance: {"name":"","age":200,"nickname":"Ash"} -> 3 violations:
1. $.name: String is shorter than minLength 1.
2. $.age: Number 200 is greater than the maximum 150.
3. $: Additional property 'nickname' is not allowed.
